findings.title: A card refund sends money back to the card before servd checks the refund policy, caps or approver role
findings.scenario: `POST /pos/terminal/refunds` is open to MANAGERS. That list includes role `manager`, which is NOT in OVERRIDE_APPROVERS. startTerminalRefund only checks the refundable amount, then pushToMachine calls `driver.refund`, so the machine gives the money back. Only afterwards does recordRefund call refundOrder, which runs `ensureCapOrManagerOverride` (cashier cap, manager cap, photo-evidence policy) and `assertRefundable`. Reproduced on the review DB: a `manager` user refunded PKR 500 of a card_terminal payment. The test driver's refund was called once, then refundOrder threw MANAGER_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED ('above 0'), and the charge ended in `needs_attention`. The money is back on the card, no refund Payment, ledger entry or fiscal refund exists, and the policy cap was bypassed. The same happens for any amount over managerRefundLimitCents (OVER_CAP 403), and for every card refund when requirePhotoEvidence is on (PHOTO_REQUIRED; there is no photo field in this flow).
findings.fix: Before creating the TerminalCharge and pushing, run the same refusals refundOrder will apply: getRefundPolicy(tenantId), the cap/approver/photo check from ensureCapOrManagerOverride for the actor's role, and assertRefundable(refundableOf(payments, source), amount, 'card'). Ask W4 to export a side-effect-free `assertRefundAllowed(input)` from pos/service.ts, or carry managerOverridePin/photoUrl in the body. Any refusal must be a 4xx BEFORE driver.refund is called. Add a test with role `manager` and an amount over the cap: 4xx, and the driver's refund is never called.

findings.title: BullMQ jobId reuse after `attempts` is decremented silently drops every later kick; documents stay pending
findings.scenario:
The jobId is `fiscal-<docId>-<attempts>`, and completed jobs are kept (removeOnComplete count 500). BullMQ ignores an add whose jobId still exists; verified locally, the handler ran once after two adds with the same id. sendOnce DEcrements attempts in two places: when the connector is now off (→ held) and when getConnectorFresh throws (→ pending +60 s). The next kick then reuses the jobId of the job that just completed. Scenario:
1. The CEO switches the fiscal connector off while documents are pending.
2. Sweeper-kicked jobs `fiscal-X-0` run; sendOnce leases (attempts 1), finds it off, sets held and decrements attempts to 0.
3. The CEO goes live and releases. releaseHeld calls kickFiscal(X, 0), so the jobId is `fiscal-X-0` again and the add is ignored.
4. Sweeper (c) also calls kickOrThrow(X, 0) every 30 s. The add 'succeeds' as a no-op, so the inline fallback never runs either.
The documents sit in pending (/health and the digest say 'not filed for N min') until 500 newer jobs evict the old ones. A DB blip in getConnectorFresh causes the same stall. The tests mock the kicker, so this was never exercised.
findings.fix: Make every kick unique per attempt slot. Either stop decrementing `attempts` (log the no-op instead), or build the jobId from something that always moves (for example `fiscal-<id>-<attempts>-<nextAttemptAt epoch>`, or a short random suffix; the lease already guarantees single flight), or set removeOnComplete/removeOnFail to true for this queue. Add a test with the real queue: switch off, release, and the document is sent.

findings.title: SSRF guard accepts IPv4-mapped / IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals that point at loopback or private addresses
findings.scenario:
isPrivateAddress only recognises the dotted `::ffff:a.b.c.d` form. WHATWG URL normalises `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` to `[::ffff:7f00:1]`, which falls through to 'public'. Verified with assertUrlAllowed:
- `https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/` is ALLOWED.
- `https://[::ffff:a00:1]/` (10.0.0.1) is ALLOWED.
- `https://[::127.0.0.1]/` (`::7f00:1`) is ALLOWED.
- `https://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` is ALLOWED.
The http driver's guardedLookup never runs for an IP-literal host (Node connects to it directly). An admin/IT user, or anyone with such a session, can therefore point the fiscal or terminal connector at the box's loopback or LAN services, and servd sends signed POSTs carrying the API key and the payload there.
findings.fix: Parse IPv6 to bytes (for example with net.BlockList, or a small parser) and check the embedded IPv4 for ::ffff:0:0/96, ::/96 (IPv4-compatible), 64:ff9b::/96 (NAT64) and 2002::/16 (6to4). Also reject ::/128 and ::1 in every spelling. Simplest: refuse IPv6 literals in connector URLs entirely, and in httpCall refuse any URL whose hostname is an IP literal that isPrivateAddress (after normalisation) flags. Add these URLs to the SSRF test.

findings.title: A waiting refund keeps its stale (often empty) registrations after its held sale is released, and is sent with `registrations: []`
findings.scenario:
enqueueFiscalRefundTx builds the refund payload from the sale's payload as it is at refund time. releaseHeld then REBUILDS the held sale's payload (with the new POS ids), but promoteWaitingRefunds only copies `original` into the refund. Reproduced:
1. The brand has no POS id; the sale is held/not_registered.
2. A refund is made; the refund document is waiting with registrations [].
3. The CEO adds srbPosId and releases; the sale is filed with registrations [{srb,123456}].
4. The refund is promoted to pending with registrations [] (and the seller block from before the fix).
A real vendor gets a credit note with no POS registration, so it is rejected or filed under the wrong POS.
findings.fix: In promoteWaitingRefunds, while the refund has never been attempted (attempts === 0), rebuild its payload from the sale's CURRENT payload: `buildRefundPayload(asPayload(sale.payload), { documentId: r.id, refundAmountCents: r.amountCents, issuedAt: <the original issuedAt>, reason, method, original })`, keeping the refund's own issuedAt, reason and method. At minimum copy registrations and seller. Recompute payloadHash. Add a test for this scenario.

findings.title: An approved card REFUND whose vendor amount differs is 'reversed', which pushes a second refund (or voids the refund)
findings.scenario:
In applyChargeStateTx, the approved branch sends any `state.amountCents !== c.amountCents` to void_pending + reverse, whatever the charge's kind. For a kind:'refund' charge, reverseCharge does one of two things:
- With a different Karachi day or no providerRef, it calls `driver.refund` again, so a second refund goes back to the card.
- On the same day, it voids the refund.
Either way the charge ends `voided` with no refund Payment and no alert. Reproduced: a refund charge of 40,000 got an approved webhook/poll with amountCents -40,000 (a vendor reporting refunds as negative is plausible), the clock was +26 h, the test driver's refund was called once more, and the status became voided with TERMINAL_AMOUNT_MISMATCH.
findings.fix: Gate the mismatch→reverse path on `c.kind === 'charge'`. For a refund with a mismatched amount, set `needs_attention` with refusalCode TERMINAL_AMOUNT_MISMATCH and raise `terminal_unreconciled`, and never call reverseCharge. Also make reverseCharge refuse any kind:'refund' row.

findings.title: IT can switch a LIVE fiscal connector's driver (http to test) with no CEO and no re-test; later real sales are 'filed' with TEST numbers and never re-filed
findings.scenario:
PUT /connectors/:kind (CONNECTOR_ADMINS = admin, it) only turns `enabled` off when the driver becomes 'none'. Any other driver change keeps the connector live. Scenario:
1. The company is live on 'http'.
2. An IT user PUTs `{driver:'test'}`.
3. Every following completion files through the test driver: status `filed`, isTest, a TEST-SRB-… number.
4. Those documents are final; release, retry and the sweeper never send them again, so the real sales never reach FBR/SRB.
This is an operator-level exclusion of real sales (§17.0), done by a non-CEO and outside the go-live readiness gate (including its 10-minute test requirement). Switching 'test' to 'http' likewise skips readiness.
findings.fix: While the fiscal connector is enabled, refuse a `driver` change (and arguably a `baseUrl` change) with 409 SWITCH_OFF_FIRST, so the CEO's switch-off and go-live (with its readiness check) are the only way to change the filer. Add a route test: IT changing the driver on a live fiscal connector gets 409.

findings.title: An automatic reversal by referenced refund is marked `voided` as soon as the refund is ACCEPTED, never confirmed
findings.scenario:
The TerminalDriver contract says `refund(...)` returns ok when the refund has started ('kind refund; poll like a charge'). reverseCharge treats `out.kind === 'ok'` from driver.refund (`${id}-rev`) as done: it sets `voided` and resolvedAt and never polls the reversal. Scenario:
1. A late approval arrives the next day after the order was paid by cash (cross-day, so no void is possible).
2. reverseCharge starts a referenced refund; the vendor accepts it as pending.
3. The refund later needs a card tap, or is declined or expires at the processor.
4. servd shows `voided`; no needs_attention and no terminal_void_failed alert is raised, so the customer stays charged twice.
findings.fix: For the referenced-refund path, record the reversal as its own kind:'refund' TerminalCharge (or store its providerRef). Keep the original in void_pending, or a new 'reversing' state, and poll getChargeStatus on `${id}-rev` until it is approved: then `voided`; when declined, expired or not_found, go back to backoff and on to needs_attention + terminal_void_failed. Same-day `voidCharge` (which returns {voided:true}) can stay immediate.

findings.title: Manual retry of a document that hit the 60-attempt cap gets at most one attempt, and possibly none
findings.scenario: retryDocument keeps `attempts` (for example 60). The next sendOnce leases (attempts 61), and any transient or unknown outcome makes isExhausted() true at once (`attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS`), so the document is failed again. Sweeper step (d) also selects pending rows with attempts >= 60 and fails them with no send at all if it runs before the kicked job. After a long vendor outage (the cap is reached after about 54 h, before maxAgeHours 72), 'Retry all failed' gives each document one shot, and the sweeper can re-fail some immediately.
findings.fix: Store the attempt count at retry time; the 'retry' FiscalAttempt already has attemptNo. Measure the cap as attempts since the latest retry, as the age anchor already does, both in isExhausted and in sweeper step (d).

findings.title: The legacy drain obliterates pending SRB sales-return jobs and leaves no manual_required document or flag
findings.scenario: refundOrder queues SRB returns as `{orderId, kind:'return', refundAmountCents, refundRef}` with a 5-minute delay, so any refund in the last minutes before the deploy is a 'delayed' job. drainLegacyTaxQueues collects only orderId. For an order that already has srbInvoiceNumber, it `continue`s, so the return is obliterated and only appears in the audit's orderIds list. Owner flag (e) says such a refund must become manual_required with a fiscal_manual_refund flag. It is silently lost. Low because the owner says nothing is trading yet.
findings.fix: For jobs with `data.kind === 'return'`, create a refund FiscalDocument (key `refund:<refundRef>`) as manual_required / prefiled_direct_refund with `original` = the order's srb number, plus the fiscal_manual_refund ExceptionFlag. Do this in the same way as enqueueFiscalRefundTx's no-sale-document branch.

findings.title: The §17.7 reporting-required flag can be lost by a concurrent PUT /connectors/fiscal (read-modify-write of the settings JSON)
findings.scenario:
PUT /connectors/fiscal reads `row.settings`, merges, and writes the whole JSON back, preserving fiscalReportingRequired only from the value it READ. Scenario:
1. An IT user saves fiscal settings while the CEO sets reporting-required=false.
2. The PUT read the row before the toggle, writes after it, and drops the key.
3. reportingRequiredOf falls back to TRUE.
The non-commercial company silently starts creating held documents, /health warnings and alerts again. Both writes are audited, but the state disagrees with the last audit row.
findings.fix: Do the merge atomically: either `UPDATE … SET settings = settings || $patch` with jsonb (excluding the flag), or re-read the row under `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` in a transaction in both routes. Alternatively keep the flag outside the settings blob (a Tenant column or its own Setting row).
